chapter: Riverboat to New Orleans and Horace Henderson
title: Jamming in New Orleans and the mystery trumpeter who sounded like Louis
summary: After work they jammed at places like Ramona's, finding every local trumpeter played like Armstrong; one night an unidentified tall man in overalls walked through the crowd playing like Louis.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: And you could hear the guys blowing from the other boats, you know. And then at night when you got off, then you went out and started a jam session, you know, be jamming.
What time would you get off, about midnight?
We'd get off about 12:00 or 1:00, yes, something like that. Then we would go out and find places to

blow. And that's when I found out I couldn't play nothing. I said, good God, everybody that could pick up a horn around there was playing like Louis Armstrong, and they had that tone, that great big wide tone that Louis had, had the feeling of him, you know. I never seen so many, you know, so many guys around there at that time. Well, we finally found a place where Granger and myself would go and blow, and this guy wasn't -- see, he wasn't too good, so we could blow with him. We felt a little comfortable there, you know. A little comfortable there. Then we would -- we were sitting there one night, playing. I'll never forget it. We were in a place called Ramona's down there, and we were blowing, and people weren't paying no attention to you, you know. They were dancing and drinking and we were in there, we were battling with this little buy in there, and he wasn't bad, but we figured we had a little bit over him, you know, so it's something to do, anyhow, after we got off from work.

So all at once I heard the prettiest sounds in my life coming through the crowd, and I looked up and there's this guy, tall, light skinned fellow, and I often wondered who he was. And he had on overalls, with a camel hair cap. And he took his horn out, back by the other side of -- in the back of the room, and just started walking through the crowd, blowing it, you know. And this guy was playing everything that Louis Armstrong was playing, you know. All his numbers and all the

same passages, you know, and things, and I said, "Good God, who is that?" The guys said, "Oh, man, there are a lot of guys around here. That could be one of many guys. Many guys sound just like Louis down here, you know. But the trouble about them, their reading is a little bit off, you know."
But we got -- yeah, he come up on the stand, and the first chance we got we put our horns in the bag and got out of there.

And stood back there and listened to him, because this guy was something else. I've often wondered, you know, could he be some guy, that come up later you know, and I might have met, you know, in later years.
Because I didn't know what was going on at that time, you know.
